cases.prompt: Our plant key user wants a part counter that only publishes when the counter value changes, from a connected press line. Build the Node-RED flow for our test instance.
cases.expected_output: Picks the delta gate transformation (P1) and the seven-group layout. Keeps every UUID and limit in the Set flow config node, not in function bodies. Includes the sysTime unpack and re-pack pair, clears the measured_value oneof and sets the output UUID and isDelta explicitly. Runs the analyser to zero blockers, deploys only to test and hands to acceptance; prod import goes to the human approver.

cases.prompt: A flow on our prod Node-RED instance publishes nothing and the dashboard is flat since Monday's redeploy. Here is the exported flow JSON. What is wrong?
cases.expected_output: Starts from the export and asks what changed and whether the tab is enabled. Runs the analyser and reads findings in the fixed order (secret, systime, oneof, spine-severed, threshold). Notes flow context is cleared on deploy. States what the analyser cannot see and walks outward from the machine. Fills the triage record and names the cause category; does not change anything on prod.

cases.prompt: The data from our new flow shows timestamps in the year 2262. A colleague suggests we just divide by 1000 in the function node. Should we?
cases.expected_output: Explains sysTime is a packed uint64 (seconds shifted 32 bits plus nanoseconds), not an epoch in milliseconds. Refuses the divide-by-1000 fix and points to the standard Convert sysTime and Convert sysTime back functions. Checks the unpack and re-pack pair is present on both sides (analyser systime checks).

cases.prompt: We need to decide the standard signal names and units for the temperature sensors on our new furnace before anybody builds anything.
cases.expected_output: Does not build or edit a flow. Routes the request to the signal-naming skill (mi-signals) and says a topic or signal standard must never be changed from inside a flow.
